title: Safety is Contextual, LLM-Judges Are Not: Navigating the Rigid Priors of Evaluators

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM-judges' ability to adapt to varying safety definitions that reflect diverse cultural and regional norms (e.g., restrictions on alcohol in Arabic-speaking nations vs. religious preaching in China) compared to their rigid internal safety priors.

Measuring and comparing the performance, accuracy, and F1 scores of LLM-judges across five different languages and four scripts (English, French, Japanese, Arabic, and Korean) to identify performance gaps in non-English safety evaluation.

Testing the effectiveness of LLM-judges in identifying safety violations using the MultilingualPrompts dataset, which requires niche local knowledge and understanding of region-specific concepts and slang.
